title: Outfinite Mathematics

sourceEvidence.excerpt: The programme begins from a suspicion rather than a finished foundation. Mathematics gained enormous power by idealizing away physical limits: lines need not be manufactured, functions may range over domains no computer can enumerate, and proofs can establish parametric generality without executing every case. Outfinitism does not call this success an error or demand the abolition of infinity. It asks whether distinctions normally left outside foundations should become mathematical objects when theories meet computation, measurement, organisms, institutions, and machine interpretation. These include kinds of existence, the difference between a rule and its realizations, the boundary between ideal and physical objects, and the status of an analysis stopped at a resource or observational frontier. The book distinguishes three ways of speaking about infinity. Actual infinity belongs to theories that admit completed infinite totalities and remains a coherent, productive theoretical existence. Potential infinity emphasizes an indefinitely extendable rule, but it can blur logical openness with realized continuation. Outfinite processes are proposed as a third focus: their specification has no relevant internal stopping point, yet every realized trace is finite, and every further step is an event occurring under resources, context, and a current frontier. The frontier is not merely failure. It records what has been explored, represented, measured, or computed and what remains open. A frontier-sensitive result might establish a property for all reached states, produce a counterexample, return a certified enclosure, or preserve an unresolved remainder rather than pretending to have prove

A central proposal is that existence should be typed when formal claims travel toward the world. Theoretical objects, physical instances, finite representations, computations, processes, observed phenomena, and persistent collectives require different witnesses and identity relations. A company may exist legally while failing to coordinate as an organization; a simulated entity may exist computationally without a known physical counterpart; a measured value carries instrument and error conditions absent from its ideal symbol. Theories remain local, and bridges between them become explicit hypotheses rather than invisible changes of meaning. A deductive proof establishes consequence within axioms and semantics. It does not by itself provide observation, model adequacy, implementation correctness, or empirical warrant. Provenance, approximation, measurement, statistical support, and domain

The theorem is reconstructed not as an imagined enumeration of infinitely many cases but as a finite circuit of justified transformations. Generality can be parametric: an arbitrary finite witness is handled under a declared generation or admission contract. Invariants, descent measures, counterexamples, residuals, proof terms, and certificates become typed outcomes rather than one undifferentiated label of success. Arithmetic provides an early test. Euclid’s theorem can express the extendability of every finite collection of primes; Euclid’s algorithm terminates through a decreasing finite measure; loop invariants prove familiar summation properties for arbitrary admitted inputs. Yet the framework must also distinguish mathematical integers, modular machine words, trapping arithmetic, floating point, and intervals because their operations obey different laws.
